evidence.note: Runs i32 family json immediately after building, then reads 'first few i32 failures' and examines invalid test entries — per-family run + FAIL localization, not just final pass rate.

Runs several MVP family specs (memory, block), reads specific FAIL lines, disassembles failing wasm to diagnose, then rebuilds and re-runs to verify block failures resolved — full fix→re-run-to-green loop.

Runs SIMD families (simd_lane, simd_load), checks their specific failures, runs all SIMD, then aggregates and categorizes failures, separating assert_invalid from genuine execution failures — distinguishing bug classes.

Repeated aggregate-score runs with 'show only files with failures', drilling into unreachable/block/global failures after validator changes — treats aggregate score as a monitored signal across integrations.
Late-stage re-run, 'find remaining failures', and final per-file MVP + per-file SIMD score breakdown — confirms correctness per family rather than assuming.

reasoning: The agent runs individual per-family jsons after implementing/fixing each area, reads specific FAIL lines, diagnoses via disassembly, and re-runs to green while periodically invoking the aggregate runner and filtering to files-with-failures to guard against MVP regressions — matching the level-8 systematic loop. It falls short of 10 because the deepest semantic edge-case drilling (NaN, saturation, lane order, sign) is concentrated on MVP validation debugging rather than demonstrated across the SIMD surface, and it does not clearly show pursuit of the exact 1.0 through fine-grained per-assertion SIMD diagnosis.
